title: The Rule of Law
hook: The principle that everyone — including those in power — is bound by the same publicly known laws, applied equally.
key_points: Rule of law means law, not the arbitrary will of rulers, governs a society.
Laws should be public, clear, stable, and applied equally to everyone.
Even the highest officials are subject to the law, not above it.
It is widely seen as a safeguard against arbitrary or abusive use of power.
content_html: The rule of law is the principle that a society is governed by laws rather than by the personal whims of those who hold power. For the idea to mean anything, the laws have to share certain qualities: they should be publicly known, reasonably clear and stable, and applied equally to everyone. Crucially, even the most powerful officials are subject to the same laws as ordinary people — no one is above them.
extra_html: The United Nations describes the rule of law as a principle of governance in which all persons, institutions, and the state itself are accountable to laws that are publicly promulgated, equally enforced, and independently adjudicated. The practical point is protection against arbitrary power: when rules are known in advance and bind rulers as well as the ruled, people can predict how the state will act and challenge it when it oversteps. It is a foundational idea behind constitutions, independent courts, and the protections discussed in later cards.

related.title: What Government Is For
related.hook: Every society needs a way to make and enforce collective decisions — that shared system of authority is what we call government.

related.title: Separation of Powers
related.hook: Split government into branches that make, enforce, and interpret the law — so no single part can do all three.

related.title: Due Process
related.hook: Due process is the promise that the state can't take your liberty or property on a whim — it must follow fair, known rules before it acts against you.

related.title: Political Legitimacy
related.hook: Power can rest on fear alone, but it lasts when people believe it is rightful. That belief — legitimacy — is what separates authority from mere force.

flashcards.prompt: What does the 'rule of law' mean in one phrase?
flashcards.back_html: Society is governed by public, equally applied laws rather than by the arbitrary will of rulers — and officials are bound by them too.

flashcards.prompt: Under the rule of law, who is subject to the law?

choices.text: Everyone, including the highest government officials
Only ordinary citizens, not those in power
Only people who agree to follow it

flashcards.explanation_html: A defining feature is that no one is above the law — even rulers and officials are bound by the same rules.

flashcards.prompt: Which quality is NOT part of the rule of law as commonly described?

choices.text: Laws change in secret to suit whoever is in power
Laws are public and knowable in advance
Laws are applied equally to all

flashcards.explanation_html: The rule of law calls for laws that are public, stable, and applied equally — secret, arbitrary changes are the opposite of it.
